summary.text: A neutron star merger is the collision of two neutron stars that spiral together as their orbit loses energy to gravitational radiation.
The result is either a heavier neutron star or a black hole, along with a short gamma-ray burst and a kilonova glow.
These collisions forge a large share of the elements heavier than iron, through a process called the r-process.

facts.label: GW170817
facts.value: Seen on 17 August 2017 in galaxy NGC 4993

facts.label: Gamma-ray delay
facts.value: Burst arrived 1.7 seconds after the wave signal

facts.label: Heavy elements
facts.value: About half the isotopes heavier than iron

facts.label: Magnetic field
facts.value: Trillions of times stronger than Earth's, within milliseconds

items.prompt: Two neutron stars circle each other. Why do they slowly drift closer together?

options.label: They lose energy as gravitational radiation
They are pulled by a third nearby star
They cool and shrink while orbiting
Their magnetic fields attract them

items.explain: Spiralling inward happens because energy is emitted as gravitational radiation.

items.prompt: After two neutron stars merge, what decides whether a black hole forms?

options.label: How bright the gamma-ray burst is
Whether the remnant's mass exceeds a limit
How far from Earth the event happened
Which of the two stars was spinning faster

items.explain: A more massive neutron star results unless the remnant's mass exceeds the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit, in which case a black hole forms.

items.prompt: Gold and other heavy elements need a very dense flood of neutrons to form. Why do neutron star mergers matter here?

options.label: They scatter gold from older planets
They briefly supply extreme neutron flux
They cool matter into solid metals
They collect dust into gold-rich clouds

items.explain: A merger briefly creates such extreme neutron flux that the r-process can occur, accounting for about half the isotopes heavier than iron.

items.prompt: Waves and light from GW170817 arrived within seconds of each other, from the same spot. What did this establish?

options.label: That neutron star mergers produce short gamma-ray bursts
That all gamma-ray bursts come from mergers
That the Hubble constant is exactly known
That black holes never form from mergers

items.explain: The gamma-ray burst coincided with the gravitational wave in both space and time, which established that these mergers produce short bursts.

items.prompt: Why was the glow found 11 hours after GW170817 so important?

options.label: It proved the merger was in our galaxy
It showed that neutron stars are made of light
It had kilonova characteristics, linking mergers to kilonovae
It ended the event right away

items.explain: Its expected kilonova characteristics showed that neutron star mergers are responsible for kilonovae.

items.prompt: A radio operator wants to know which signal from a merger arrives first at Earth. What is the order?

options.label: Cosmic rays, then gamma rays, then waves
Gamma rays, then waves, then cosmic rays
Waves first, then gamma-ray photons, then cosmic ray particles
All of them arrive at the same moment

items.explain: Gravitational waves arrive first, the burst and afterglow photons seconds to hours after, and cosmic ray particles hundreds to thousands of years later.
